flow.description: The first upstream (kept for 1.0 payloads and the run details link).

flows.description: Every upstream; empty for rows written before fan-in existed.

key.description: Parameter that identifies a batch: the downstream runs once per value.

ArtifactListItem.description: One artifact in the cross-run listing, with its run's identity.

ArtifactRow.description: A stored artifact attached to a run and optionally a task run.

interval.description: Seconds, or a shorthand like `1d`, `12h`, `30m`. Default one day.

filter.description: The same filters as `GET /api/runs`, as an object; empty matches every run.

affected.description: Runs the action applied to: every match for delete, non-terminal ones for cancel, terminal ones for rerun.

matched.description: Runs the filter matched, capped at 10,000.

secret.description: True when the value is set and hidden.

source_name.description: The flag, variable, `app.serve()` argument, or table and key.

value.description: The value in effect; null when nothing sets it or it is secret.

active.description: Number of non-terminal runs held in memory.

flows.description: Run counts by flow id and state type.

task_runs.description: Task run counts by state type.

CreateRunBody.description:
Create a run by flow key, registering the flow when the server does not
know it yet (offline handoff from another project).

flow_group.description: The flow's declared group; absent leaves the registered group as it is.

backup_dir.description: Where a reset writes its copy.

stale_projects.description: Projects none of whose flows this server serves.

DeletedCounts.description: Rows deleted by a project removal or a reset.

DownstreamSkip.description: A flow that runs after the skipped one, directly or further down its chain.

fires.description: The skipped fires whose runs of this flow will be created Skipped.

cereyan_toml.description: The served directory's `cereyan.toml` with its secrets hidden.

cereyan_unset.description: Known `CEREYAN_*` variables that are not set.

seq.description: Sequence number: the writer assigns ids in commit order.

name.description: The name a rule matches on, e.g. `run.failed`.

payload_fields.description: The payload keys the emit site sets.

resource.description: The resource kind the event hangs off.

when.description: One sentence on when the engine records it.

Expectation.description: An armed expectation of a proactive rule.

Flow.description: A registered flow. Identity is `(project, name)`.

group.description:
The group the flow is listed under, declared in Python with `group=`.
Null means none was declared and the flow is grouped under its project;
API responses carry the resolved value, so clients never apply that
fallback themselves.

live.description: Whether the running server has this flow registered from code.

FlowOptions.description: Flow-level options declared in Python and stored as JSON on the flow row.

start_deadline.description: Seconds a run may wait to start before it is skipped; a schedule's own value wins.

batch_key.description: The batch key of a keyed fan-in.

recent_runs.description:
Newest first: (run id, state type, state name, duration in microseconds
or null while the run has none) of the last ten runs.

triggered_by.description: The flow this one runs after, if any (the first upstream).

triggers.description: Flows that run after this one.

upstreams.description: Every upstream of a fan-in flow (empty without `after=`).

active_runs.description: Runs that are Pending, Running, Paused or Cancelling.

matching_rules.description: Rules whose match names the project; they are kept.

last_run_at.description: Start time of the project's latest run.

live_flows.description: Flows this server registered from code.

served.description: True when any of its flows is live, so it cannot be removed.

ProjectedFire.description: A fire past the look-ahead, computed from the schedule; no run exists for it yet.

backup.description: Write a copy to `<home>/backups/` first; defaults to true.

backup_path.description: The copy written before the reset, when one was asked for.

input.description: The answer handed to `wait_for_input` on the resumed attempt (any JSON).

source.description: Where the handler is defined (module and function), for the settings page.

RuleAction.description: One rule action. `kind` selects the variant; other fields are optional.

callable.description: Name of the Python callable for `call` actions (code rules).

secret.description: Webhook signing secret (Standard Webhooks headers when set).

RuleClock.description: Clock of a clock-armed proactive rule: a cron expression in a timezone.

events.description: Event names, or prefixes ending in `*`.

after_consecutive.description: Fire only on an event whose `failures_in_a_row` is at least this; 0 is off.

oneOf.description: Clock-armed rules: evaluate at each cron tick instead of on an event.
Proactive rules: the expected event that disarms an expectation.

within.description: Seconds after the arming event (or look-back before a clock tick).

attributes.description: Searchable key-values the run set on itself with `set_attributes`.

group.description: The flow's group, read through the flow: never stored on the run.

task_counts.description: Task runs of this run counted by state type; empty until tasks exist.

config_file.description: The served directory's `cereyan.toml`, when it has one.

Sample.description: One point of the dashboard's history.

oneOf.description: Anchor time in microseconds UTC; defaults to the schedule's creation.

catchup_window.description: Seconds; missed fires older than this are not caught up. 0 or absent is off.

jitter.description: Seconds; each run is due up to this long after its fire time.

start_deadline.description: Seconds; a run not started this long after it was due is skipped. 0 or absent is off.

ScheduleRow.description:
Placeholders for later phases; defined now so the schema and API types
are stable from the start.
A stored schedule row: the schedule itself plus policy and bookkeeping.

catchup_window.description: Seconds: missed fires older than this are not caught up. None is off.

jitter.description: Seconds: each run becomes due up to this long after its fire time.

oneOf.description: Next fire that will run, computed by the scheduler (not stored).

skipped.description: Future fires skipped by a person, counted by the scheduler (not stored).

source.description:
`code` for schedules declared on the flow, `ui` for ones created in the
interface, `mcp` for ones created by an agent. Startup reconciliation
singles out `code` alone; every other value is left as it is.

start_deadline.description: Seconds: a run that has not started this long after it was due is skipped.

base_path.description: URL path every TCP route is served under; empty at the root.

exposed.description: Bound beyond loopback with no token required.

title.description: UI title in effect: `[ui] title` from cereyan.toml, or `cereyan`.

token_file.description: The file holding the generated token when the server generated one.

url.description: Dialable URL including the base path, with no trailing slash.

backup_every.description: Hours between scheduled backups; 0 is off.

keep_last_runs_per_flow.description: Runs per flow retention never deletes.

last_backup_at.description: Microseconds since the epoch of the last backup, scheduled or on demand.

retain_failed_runs_days.description: Days to keep Failed and Crashed runs; 0 means `retain_runs_days`.

retain_runs_days.description: Days to keep terminal runs; 0 keeps them.

title.description: UI title in effect: `[ui] title` from cereyan.toml, or `cereyan`.
UI title; an empty string removes `[ui] title` and restores `cereyan`.

fires.description: Fire times to skip, in microseconds, as the upcoming list gives them.

next.description: Skip the next N fires not already skipped instead.

state_type.description: For a sub-state, the type it belongs to; for a type, itself.

TableCounts.description: Row counts for the Data tab and the reset dialog.

parents.description: External ids of task runs this one waited on (futures and wait_for).

pass.description:
Which execution of the run's body created this task run: 0 for the
first, the next for a resume or an in-process flow retry. Dynamic keys
restart with each pass, so the pass tells repeated calls apart.

UpcomingItem.description: One entry of the upcoming list: a run, or with `projected=N` a fire without one.

projected.description: Always false: this fire has a run.

skipped.description: A person skipped this fire: the run ends Skipped at its time instead of starting.

skipped_at.description: When it was skipped, in microseconds, when `skipped`.

UpcomingRun.description: A materialized run in the upcoming list.

value.description: Plain JSON value, or `"********"` for secrets in API responses.

raw.description: Ciphertext of a secret, present only when `raw=true` was requested.

events.description: Every engine-emitted event, in catalogue order.

reserved_prefixes.description:
Prefixes the engine owns. A name under one of these must be an entry in
`events`; any other name is a custom event and is never checked.

states.description:
Every value a rule's `states` accepts: the types then the sub-states. A
rule naming a type also matches that type's sub-states.

pass.description:
Which execution of the run's body this is: 0 the first time, the next
after a resume. The engine counts its own retries up from here and
reports it with every task run it creates.

report_seq.description:
The last report sequence the store recorded for this run. A fresh engine
process buffers from zero, and the store skips any event at or below the
run's sequence as a redelivery, so an engine picking up a run someone
else already reported on has to continue that count rather than restart
it. Without this a resumed run's whole report was silently dropped.
